title: Support for roughnotation on parts of LaTeX/math expressions
description:
First of all, thank you for creating and maintaining the `quarto-roughnotation` extension. It is a very elegant and useful way to visually emphasize content in Quarto documents, especially for teaching and presentations.

While using it in lecture slides (revealjs), I noticed that the extension currently does not support applying roughnotation to _parts of mathematical expressions_. It works well for plain text, but there seems to be no straightforward way to annotate or highlight specific subexpressions inside LaTeX math, e.g.

```
$$
a + b + c
$$
```
where one might want to annotate only b, or perhaps a full subexpression like b + c.

This would be extremely valuable for step-by-step derivations in mathematics, and physics, where emphasizing specific terms inside equations is pedagogically important.

I understand that this may be technically nontrivial due to how MathJax/KaTeX renders equations into HTML. Still, I wanted to ask:

- Is there currently a recommended workaround?
- Would support for targeting math sub-elements be feasible in principle?

Thanks again for making this extension available. It’s already very useful.

Best regards,
Ralph

title: Add auto apply method for slides
a way to add the styling of the annotations without having them be fragments
Highlighting code
description:
Has anyone gotten this working for marking up parts of code on slides somehow?

It's tricky because you can't easily add CSS spans to code blocks.

Maybe someone has figured out a way to use existing tooling to do this. But if not, here are some ideas I've had, none of them fleshed out enough:

## Special comment for line below

```
# rn: print(...)
print("Hello")
```

## Special comment for current line

```
print("Hello") # rn:"Hello"
```

or `# rn:\"H.*o\"` (regex)

## cell option

` ```{.python .rn="\"Hello\""} `

or 

````
```{python}
#| rn: "Hello"
print("Hello"
```
````

title: Zooming does not work very well
description:
Thank you for providing this add in, Installation went well. I would appreciate a list of all available colours somewhere in the examples slides. A major issue for me is that if I put the browser in full screen mode and zoom, I can't find a zoom option where the alignment is good. Seems to depend on the width of my monitors, one works fine, the other one doesn't. I can't use this add-in if I can't expect it to work well depending on the projector. Is there something one can add to the YAML to give the presentation specific dimensions perhaps? Thanks again, Code: `--- title: "Reprex (on my screens at least)" format: revealjs filters: - roughnotation --- ## Title [Word]{.rn rn-color=yellow rn-index=1} and [another word]{.rn rn-index=2 rn-color=lightgreen}
[A third word]{.rn rn-index=2 rn-color=lightblue} and [a fourth]{.rn rn-color=yellow rn-index=1}` ![image](https://github.com/EmilHvitfeldt/quarto-roughnotation/assets/7349924/db02985a-e511-4151-86b4-1df8dd7fdc25)

title: [Feature request] Add option to annotate using next button
description: It would be great to add an option so that an end user could have annotations added as a 'next slide', transitioning in similarly to fragments, instead of needing to press 'R'. This is especially useful in contexts where a presentation remote is being used. Not sure if this is possible given Quarto's extension format, however.

title: Marking to identify when RN is present on slide
description:
Am loving integrating this into my Quarto decks! I wonder if there's a way to place a small identifier on the slide when notations are present on that slide. Perhaps a little dot in a corner, for example, that is one color when RNs are present on the slide and have *not* been activated, and have it change colors or disappear when all RNs have been triggered.

Thank you, again, for a wonderful Quarto addition!
